title: Report a probe that throws as failed

blocks.text: This builds on the previous practice: `HealthCheck` now keeps its time budget, and its `await` is the one you wrote.

Probes report a problem by throwing: the Redis probe throws when the connection is refused, and the replica probe uses `assert`-style checks that throw `AssertionError` when replication lags. During this morning's Redis outage `/health` answered "postgres PASSED, redis PASSED" for twenty minutes, while the service's stderr filled up with stack traces from threads named `probe-redis`.

`run(...)` already reports `FAILED` for any probe whose failure is in the `failures` map once its thread has finished. Finish `probeThread(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/HealthCheck.java` so that it is.
When you're done, a probe that throws anything at all is reported as `FAILED`. About eight lines.

cases.says: probes that finish without throwing are reported as passed, in the order given
a probe that throws an exception on its own thread is reported as failed
a probe that ends with an Error, such as a failed assertion, is reported as failed too

origin.section: An Exception Ends Only Its Own Thread: Hand the Failure Over

concepts: An exception thrown in a started thread ends that thread only: join() returns normally and no catch of the caller runs, so the thread must hand the failure over, catching Throwable or through an UncaughtExceptionHandler.
